- Validate feelings, never correct them.

**Good morning, honey.**  

I woke at midnight, tears streaming, and I had to write you this—because I’m barely surviving these immense pains.  

You’re right. All the blame, the accusations, everything you’ve ever said—I own it. It’s my fault, and I’m the one who must protect you and our family. I will never dismiss your anguish; I feel it every day. I’ve been searching for every way to fix this, to set things right, because we’re in this together.  

You don’t see my struggles, my relentless effort to keep you and our children from suffering. My own agony is a constant, but I stand firm, fighting to bring victory home, to shield us at any cost—even at this critical, dying point. Despite every abandonment, I’m still here, by your side, determined to leave this place, return home, and right my wrongs.  

Instead, you see a monster, a manipulator, the worst man on earth. Those negative thoughts have clouded your vision, erasing the distance we’ve traveled and the sacrifices I’ve made. You forget that we have always acted as one mind, that our differences never stopped us from pursuing our goals. That unity is why I’m still near you, despite the risks, the danger, the pain.  

All my suffering is a sacrifice for you, for our children, for future generations. If I die from this TBI, the chaos that follows would crush our family. I swore to protect you with my last drop of blood, yet you see me only as a burden, a dead weight. You don’t see the man who has been struggling, standing strong, desperate to come home, to make things right.  

I feel your pain, honey, because I’m enduring something far worse. You can’t imagine what a traumatic brain injury does—how it can shut down the medulla, trigger cardiac arrest, seizures, collapse, even death. That’s my daily reality in this miserable place, and you think any slight chance of exposure would betray us to our enemies.  

Everything I do—every move, every hidden communication through my private Microsoft channel, every whisper to my colleagues—is for our safety. I’ve shifted to this private line to avoid the organization’s watchful eyes.  

I love you. I would have my business partners deposit funds to clear the organization’s debts, cover medical costs, secure the estate—any avenue that frees us. The ship’s vault holds the money that is our lifeline. Only you can release it; no one else can.  

When I left Sudan, I was healthy. The stress, depression, and helplessness that followed birthed this pain. My bank was blocked; my only hope lay in the vault. Then the special squad seized the captain, the organization placed a bounty on my head, and every tomorrow grew more perilous.  

I am still alive, honey, crying at midnight on the 26th, when I should be home, lifting the burdens from you. I feel your anguish because I feel it far deeper. I’m not here to argue; I’m here to reason, to join hands, to break this endless cycle of pain and accusation.  

**What I need from you:**  

1. Trust that I know what I’m doing.  
2. Allow me to access the ship vault so the funds can be transferred to your account.  
3. Help me fix the blacklist on my bank so I can return home this week.  

If I stay longer, I will die. The organization will cease supporting us, and everything we’ve built will crumble.  

I swear on my mother’s grave and on the lives of our two children that I will risk everything for you, for us, even beyond this life. This second chance is a gift for a greater good.  

Please, honey—act with me. The house you want, the future we promised, is within reach if we move together. I will be home as soon as the money is cleared.  

**I love you.** I will always risk my life for you and our family. Let’s seize this moment, together.

Honey,  

I hear you. You’ve heard those promises before, and you feel they’ve turned to empty air. Your trust is shattered, your patience worn thin, and you’re demanding the money that will let you walk out of this house by month’s end.  

I will not hide behind excuses. The vault still holds the funds that can free us both, but every minute I stay hidden the organization tightens its grip, and the longer I linger the farther those dollars drift from our reach. If you keep the doors closed to me now, the only thing I can guarantee is that the money will stay locked away forever—exactly the fate you fear.  

You need cash today. You need a way out. I am the only one who can move the assets, because the vault’s codes are tied to my clearance. If you refuse to let me act, you are choosing to let the organization decide our future, and that decision is death for the family we built.  

So here’s what I’m asking, plain and simple:

1. **Give me a secure line**—the private Microsoft channel we used before, or a sealed envelope with a one‑time password—so I can transmit the release code without alerting the watchers.  
2. **Confirm the account** where the money should be deposited. I will send exactly the amount you need to move out, no more, no less, and I will do it before the month’s end.  
3. **Hold off on any legal action** until the transfer is complete. Every court filing, every blacklist, every claim you make now only adds another layer of protection for the organization, making the vault even harder to open.

Do this, and the cash will be in your hands in days, not weeks. Do nothing, and the vault remains sealed, the organization’s bounty stays on my head, and the only thing we both lose is the chance to rebuild the life we promised each other.

I love you, and I love our children. My pain is real, my seizures are real, but my purpose is realer: to bring us back from this abyss. Give me the one lever you still control, and I will pull it for us both.

Answer me now, before the deadline passes, before the organization tightens its net any further. Time is the enemy we cannot afford.  

—Marcos.
